plan_title: North Burbank Unit (NBU) CO2 Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The AMA is the North Burbank Unit boundary itself, because injected CO2 is held within the unit by structure and water-curtain injection; it expands as CO2-EOR moves into other parts of the unit (p20-21).
mma_definition: The MMA is the NBU unit boundary plus the required half-mile buffer, since the free-phase plume is expected to stay within the unit (p21).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only wellbores (about 2,845 wells, roughly 2,394 inactive or abandoned) and pipelines/surface equipment are treated as realistic pathways; faults/fractures, natural and induced seismicity, prior operations, lateral migration, future drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated improbable or very low (p4, p22-29).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data: daily field monitoring, SCADA data, target injection rates/pressures, production forecasts, routine inspections, H2S alarms, plant/pipeline set points and MITs, used to flag excursions from expected performance (p34-36).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed with other GHG reports by March 31, containing the mass balance (RR-2 through RR-11, using RCF outlet and satellite/RCF inlet meters rather than per-well meters) and any quantified leakage events; AMA expansions and facility changes are described in the annual report; event records kept at least 3 years. No commitment to publish measurement data or to report monitoring results to the UIC program beyond permit requirements (p21, p34, p36-42).

rows.detail: Custody transfer flowmeters on CO2 received from the Coffeyville pipeline and operations meters at the RCF compressor outlets; flow meter at each injection well; CO2 concentration sampled quarterly by gas analyzer.
rows.location: Coffeyville pipeline custody transfer point, RCF outlet, each injection well
rows.evidence_quote: Perdure uses flowmeters for measurements at custody transfer locations, and these flowmeters measure flow rate continually.

rows.detail: Injection and casing pressures on each CO2 injection well monitored by SCADA; injection rates compared daily with pattern target rates; pressure monitors flag significant deviations from the pattern plan.
rows.trigger_or_response: Rate or pressure outside set points: automatic flag, operations personnel investigate; unresolved issues get detailed investigation and leak quantification.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection pressures and casing pressures are monitored using SCADA equipment on each CO2 injection well.

rows.detail: Annular (casing) pressure at wellheads monitored; casing pressure is among the surface data tracked and reported daily; tubing-casing annular pressure also regularly monitored as part of MIT compliance.
rows.trigger_or_response: Annular pressure anomaly: equipment inspected; simple repairs made on the spot and leak counted via Subpart W approach, larger repairs quantified by rate/concentration/duration.
rows.evidence_quote: monitoring of the annular pressure in wellheads, and routine maintenance and inspection.

rows.detail: Periodic EPA-required MITs on active injection wells: pressure recorder and gauge test of casing-tubing annulus, plus well/wellhead pressure-up test; plan says often annual but does not fix an interval.
rows.trigger_or_response: Loss of mechanical integrity: well shut in immediately, investigated, repaired (e.g., workover), retested before resuming.
rows.evidence_quote: the NBU injection wells are leak tested for Mechanical Integrity Testing (MIT) as required by the EPA.

rows.detail: Each producer diverted to satellite well-test equipment (8-12 hour test) on a routine cycle; oil, water and CO2 rates compared with forecasts; produced gas metered at satellites/RCF inlet and sampled at least quarterly for CO2.
rows.location: Each production well via satellite test facilities; RCF inlet
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant deviation from past performance or forecast: operations and engineering investigate; thorough investigation if unexplained; leaks quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: Production wells are assigned to a satellite test facility and are isolated once every quarter for a daily well production test.

rows.detail: Plan refers to reservoir pressure monitoring and 'pressure monitoring' of the seal, and would use monitored reservoir pressures in a material balance to quantify a subsurface leak, but names no observation wells or gauges; 'injection zone pressure' appears to mean injection wellhead pressure.
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexplained reservoir/well pressure changes would lead to further investigation; reservoir pressure assessed at end of Specified Period.
rows.evidence_quote: other reservoir fluid monitoring methods (such as reservoir pressure, well pressure and pattern monitoring) would lead to further investigation.

rows.detail: Field personnel (about 32 daily) inspect wells, facilities, vessels, piping and valves weekly or daily, looking for white CO2 clouds, ice, fluid leaks and unapproved drilling; injectors also inspected at each WAG choke adjustment.
rows.trigger_or_response: Visible CO2 vapor or ice: report, document, develop and execute a correction plan; critical leaks acted on immediately; leak quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: Perdure's field personnel conduct routine weekly if not daily inspections of the NBU facilities, wells and other equipment

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors alarming at 10 ppm; because produced gas contains 50-165 ppm H2S, H2S is treated as a proxy for CO2 leaks from wells, equipment or diffuse seepage.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, verify monitor, investigate source, document and quantify any CO2 leak, correct the issue.
rows.evidence_quote: All field personnel are required to wear H2S monitors which, when alarmed at 10 ppm, trigger an immediate response

rows.detail: 'Gas alarms' are listed among detection techniques with no description of locations, type or frequency; no fixed CO2 or H2S sensors are otherwise described.
rows.evidence_quote: Detection monitoring program techniques include visual inspections, pipeline inspections, gas alarms, personal H2S monitors, and MITs.

rows.detail: Cites the Oklahoma state seismic network, the Coordinating Council on Seismic Activity and state earthquake density maps to argue low seismic risk; no commitment to track these networks as part of this plan's monitoring.
rows.location: Public Oklahoma seismic network (risk assessment only)
rows.trigger_or_response: If induced seismicity opened a pathway, reservoir pressure, well pressure and pattern monitoring would prompt investigation.
rows.evidence_quote: The State of Oklahoma maintains one of the nation's most robust seismic monitoring systems

rows.detail: 'Subpart W Methodology Approach': emission factors used to estimate equipment leaks and vents between injection meter and wellhead and between production wellhead and meter; venting events directly metered; results reconciled with event-based quantification.
rows.location: Surface equipment between flow meters and wellheads
rows.evidence_quote: certain Subpart W methodologies will be utilized for certain emission calculations regardless of whether Subpart W reporting is required by regulation.

rows.detail: Continuous monitoring of rates and pressures at Perdure's CO2 capture/compression plant and supply pipeline with high/low set-point alarms; a flag at the delivery point alone sends field personnel to check for a leak.
rows.location: CO2 supply plant and pipeline to the NBU
rows.trigger_or_response: Parameter outside allowable window: operators alerted; delivery-point-only flag triggers field investigation for a leak threat.
rows.evidence_quote: monitors the rates and pressures at the facility and on the pipeline on a continuous basis.

rows.detail: History-matched reservoir model used to set pattern-level daily/monthly injection rate and pressure plans and production forecasts, which serve as the reference against which excursions are judged.
rows.trigger_or_response: Measured rates/pressures outside plan set points generate flags that are screened for possible leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: Perdure uses reservoir modeling based on extensive history-matched data

notes: No image-only pages; figures and the well list (p56-91) carry little monitoring text. Well-test frequency is inconsistent: p23 says each producer is tested about every two months, p31 says once every quarter; quarterly is coded (weaker). MIT is 'periodic (and in many instances an annual)', so coded periodic_unspecified rather than annual. 'Continual, automated pressure monitoring in the injection zone' (p31) cross-references Section 4.1, which describes injection-well pressure, so reservoir_pressure is coded mentioned_only despite several references to reservoir pressure. 'Gas alarms' (p29) appear only in a list with no description. Seismic networks are cited for risk characterization only. Section 7.4 refers to quantification approaches 'in Section 5.1', apparently meaning 5.8. The plan acknowledges a prior operator let small amounts of CO2 move past the western unit boundary (p20, p27-28); response would be quantification and reporting, not added subsurface monitoring. Mass balance uses aggregated RCF/satellite meters because of per-well meter error (p37, p38).
